lines.en: Yoo Joonghyuk's master, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, was patient.
She had been that way 100 years ago, and 200 years ago.
That was how she had established her own school (一家) of swordsmanship.
Even when countless martial artists sold their martial arts and left Murim, she had remained here alone and broken through to the realm of transcendence.
“So, just what the hell are you?”
Poke. Poke.

An enormous finger jabbed Yoo Joonghyuk's cheek again and again as he dangled in midair. It was only a finger, but it belonged to a transcendent. Naturally, it hurt. Yet Yoo Joonghyuk gave no reaction.
「“Like master, like disciple. That bitch and that bastard are exactly alike.”」
Those were words the Heavenly Demon, one of Murim's ten greatest masters, had once spoken.
Perhaps the Heavenly Demon had judged them accurately.
“Not even a single word in reply. If you won't speak, I'll spank you.”
With those words, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint raised her enormous tobacco pipe.
With the acupoints throughout his body sealed, Yoo Joonghyuk couldn't move at all, and his backside made a pitiful smacking sound.
‘Damn you, Kim Dokja. I will kill you.’
Smack! Smack! Smack!
The sound seemed playful, but the internal power behind it was no joke.
Before long, a trickle of blood appeared at the corner of Yoo Joonghyuk's mouth.
At that point, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's delicate eyebrows curved strangely.
“You live up to that face of yours.”
She sounded somewhat impressed.
“I'll ask you again. Just where did you secretly learn the Breaking the Sky Sword School's martial arts?”
“Tell me honestly, and I'll spare your life.”
At those words, Yoo Joonghyuk slowly raised his head.
The Breaking the Sky Sword School's martial arts were not to be taught to outsiders (非人不傳). As an outsider, Yoo Joonghyuk should never have learned them.
Yet the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had said she would spare his life.
Her meaning was clear.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint intended to take Yoo Joonghyuk as her disciple.
‘Master.’
Yoo Joonghyuk understood his master's feelings better than anyone.
In a declining Murim, finding a proper disciple was difficult.
Then a transcendent versed in martial arts of the same school as hers had suddenly appeared.
Naturally, she would be interested.
Yoo Joonghyuk bit his lip.
Perhaps it wouldn't be so bad to go along with Kim Dokja's intentions here.
He knew the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, Namgung Minyoung, better than anyone.
If he waited for an opening and brought up the right things, he could surely win her favor.
But he didn't want to do that.
“Hmm, your eyes burn like fire.”
“Could you be in love with me?”
Spouting such nonsense at a time like this—she was definitely his master.
Yoo Joonghyuk bit down hard on his lip.
‘If you meet me here, you'll die.’
Yoo Joonghyuk remembered the last time he had seen his master's back.
A transcendent, wounded and twisted in solitude after long years of grueling training.
Someone who had stubbornly refused to yield, no matter what happened.
―You foolish disciple. These aren't opponents you can face.
His master, fighting the Returnee Alliance alone as the Heavenly Demon and the Blood Demon, Murim's strongest, attacked her together.
―Live, Joonghyuk.
Back then, Yoo Joonghyuk had been unable to fight beside her.
Because he was weak.
Because he was too weak.
“······Your eyes are sad.”
The sudden voice made Yoo Joonghyuk flinch.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's clear eyes reflected Yoo Joonghyuk.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, Namgung Minyoung, was half human and half giant.
Thus, this was one of the abilities of the Neanderthal giants.
“Lonely, arrogant, and deeply wounded.”
Mirror Eyes (明鏡目), which could read the emotions of others.
Through those eyes, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint was looking inside Yoo Joonghyuk.
“Just who are you?”
In pain, as though every part of him were being laid bare, Yoo Joonghyuk bit his lip hard.
He mustn't speak.
Absolutely not a word······.
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ looks at you.]
At that message, Yoo Joonghyuk looked up into the air.
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ says it will be all right.]
······It would be all right?
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ says this round will be different.]
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ tells you to trust your master.]
This round was different.
Had anyone else said that, he wouldn't have believed it.
But why?
Somehow, he wanted to believe what that guy said.
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’······.]
“That gnat······ is noisy.”

The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint flicked a finger into the air, and with a tzzzt, every sound around them vanished. She had cut off the sound with magic. A transcendent at her level could do even that, if only briefly.
Unless a dokkaebi adjusted the channel's frequency, Kim Dokja's voice would remain inaudible for a while.
From now on, he had to rely on his own judgment.
“······My name is Yoo Joonghyuk.”
After briefly steadying his breathing, Yoo Joonghyuk drew in a breath.
“I was your disciple.”
“Hmm······ What does that mean? I've never seen anyone like you. And I certainly have no memory of taking you as my disciple.”
“Exactly what I said. I learned martial arts from you······.”
Just as Yoo Joonghyuk was about to continue, sparks erupted all over his body.
[The Story ‘Disciple of Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’ is activating.]
Yoo Joonghyuk's lips twisted against his will, changing the ending of his sentence.
Yoo Joonghyuk's expression contorted.
He recalled a conversation with the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint in the previous round.
―You said you were a ‘regressor.’ Then perhaps you'll meet me again someday.
―I'm not being your disciple in the next round.
―Such a sharp-tongued brat. If only you'd speak a little more nicely······ When will you ever learn to address me respectfully? In your next life?
Perhaps this Story had remained because of that conversation with the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
[You must use respectful speech when addressing the incarnation ‘Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.’]
It was absurd.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint who had been with him then was gone.
Yet this Story still remained with him.
―When that time comes, be my disciple again.
Emotion surged, and old memories poured down like a waterfall, pounding at his heart.
He couldn't hear the indirect messages, but he could feel Kim Dokja watching him.
‘A companion.’
Yoo Joonghyuk had long forgotten what it felt like to trust someone.
He blinked slowly, then spoke.
“Do you wish to know who I am?”
“Of course I do. Very much.”
“Then I will open my mental barrier. Look inside me. Your Mirror Eyes should make that possible.”
“······Hmm. You know about Mirror Eyes, too?”
“Exactly five minutes. I cannot give you any longer.”
Suspicion entered the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's eyes.
“You're not plotting some strange trick, are you?”
“Even if I were, wouldn't you be able to subdue me anyway?”
At his almost provocative tone, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's eyebrows twitched.
“Very well.”
Constellations weren't the only ones who loved stories.
And chances to glimpse another transcendent's existence were rare.
A transcendent who had suddenly appeared in Murim, using the same martial arts as her.
How could she not be curious?
“I will look at you.”
Then the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's Mirror Eyes began to shine.
Rrrrrumble······!

Yoo Joonghyuk felt as though every hair on his head were being torn out. Transferring memories through Mirror Eyes was that dangerous. For Yoo Joonghyuk himself, and for the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint. Even so, he went through with it.
Perhaps the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's mind would break.
Perhaps she wouldn't believe what she saw.
She might reject everything and erase Yoo Joonghyuk.
But if this gamble succeeded, he might be able to change her.
The clear energy of Mirror Eyes that had engulfed their surroundings vanished only after more than ten additional minutes had passed.
Hummmmm······.
Even after the light of Mirror Eyes had faded completely, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint said nothing.
She simply kept her head bowed, staring at the floor.
Had she gone mad?
As the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint slowly raised her head, an unreadable emotion appeared in her eyes.
An expression he had never seen in all three rounds.
Only a moment later did Yoo Joonghyuk understand what it meant.
“You said you'd never become my disciple again······.”
Yoo Joonghyuk and the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint talked for a long time.
“You've been through a lot.”
“······Spare me the clumsy consolation. It doesn't suit you.”
“Good. You're definitely my disciple.”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint of the second round was dead, and would never return.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint before him was not Namgung Minyoung, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint of the second round.
Yet the two spoke as though they were unaware of that fact.
“······I avenged you. I beat both the Heavenly Demon and the Blood Demon in the 35th scenario.”
“Yes. I saw. Watching you struggle to win wasn't terribly satisfying.”
“Then why didn't you kill them yourself?”
No one would have called this a normal conversation between master and disciple.
Yet a gentle smile rested on the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's face.
“You've changed a great deal, Joonghyuk.”
“Nothing has changed.”
At that sulky reply, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint flicked a finger.
Part of the barrier formation surrounding the hut distorted, and a panel resembling the lens of a large telescope appeared. The scene outside was reflected on that small panel.
“Did you come to find me because of that child?”
There was Kim Dokja, stuffing his face with dumplings as he talked to the dog. Yoo Joonghyuk watched the scene with a frown, then opened his mouth.
“Is he a new friend?”
“He's no friend of mine. That guy is just······.”
“He's brave, already thinking of standing against the nebulas.”
“Did you think you could do it if you were with him?”

As though pleased that her taciturn disciple had finally made a friend, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint studied Kim Dokja's face through the barrier formation. Just then, part of the formation trembled, and a booming voice rang out.
[Breaking the Sky Sword Saint. It's time to hand over your martial arts.]
Startled, Yoo Joonghyuk rose to his feet.
“······A dokkaebi.”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint spoke as though thoroughly sick of it.
“The martial arts buyers have graced us with another visit.”
“······This is earlier than expected. How long has this been going on?”
“Quite a while. I'm the only one left around here now.”

Murim's martial arts had value. After all, every martial art was a kind of Story, formed through an accumulation of history. The deeper its origins, the greater its value. The dokkaebis knew that well, which was why they coveted the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's martial arts.
Yoo Joonghyuk drew [Heavenly Sword of Gathering Clouds] and spoke.
“Kim Dokja and I will take care of this.”
“Your opponents are dokkaebis. They're not beings you can handle.”
“Kim Dokja can.”
Rather than address his master's doubts, Yoo Joonghyuk studied the dokkaebi on the panel. He thought its face looked familiar, and realized it was a dokkaebi he had seen before.
‘It's that one from the Seoul Dome.’
Kim Dokja probably wouldn't leave that one alone.
Kim Dokja's voice came from beyond the screen.
―I never thought you'd still be alive. Weren't you sent off to be punished?

Sure enough, the twitch at the corner of his mouth showed that Kim Dokja had already begun his signature routine of ‘screwing someone over.’ Scratching his chin vigorously as though amused, Kim Dokja asked the growling dokkaebi a question.
―Hmm, right. You came to buy the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's martial arts?
Yoo Joonghyuk shrugged at his master.
Even without his intervention, Kim Dokja would probably settle the matter.
He didn't know how, but now that Kim Dokja was involved, he would surely pull another bizarre trick and deal the dokkaebi a solid blow.
But the next moment, Kim Dokja said something strange with an inscrutable smile.
―All right, I'll sell them. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's martial arts.
[You······ Don't tell me you're the one from back then······.]
Looking at the trembling dokkaebi's expression brought back unpleasant old memories. Biyoo, floating beside me, was frowning fiercely too.
Of course she was angry.
That dokkaebi was one of the culprits who had made the 41st round's Shin Yoosung into a ‘disaster’ and brought her down upon the Korean Peninsula, causing that tragedy.
Was its name······ ‘Paul’?
They'd definitely said it would be sent to purgatory for severe punishment, but sure enough······.
Every punishment the Bureau handed out was a slap on the wrist. How was joining the Murim redevelopment team a punishment?
“Your face has really aged since I last saw you.”
[Ugh, grrrrr······!]
“At least you were an intermediate dokkaebi back then. Now you look like······ a low-grade one?”
[You bastard! You bastard······!]

Seeing it so worked up made me sorely tempted to request another ‘private meeting’ and beat the hell out of it. I'd received a Story for beating this bastard up back then, too. Were the Wenny men still enjoying that Story on repeat?
[Enough. Step back, Paul.]
Another dokkaebi stepped forward in place of Paul, who was huffing too furiously to speak.
[Could you be ‘Kim Dokja’-nim?]
On closer inspection, this dokkaebi's face was familiar too. I'd heard that voice somewhere as well.
Huh? Wait······ This one?
“Oh, you're that one from back then, right? You worked under Bihyung······ Your name was······.”
[Youngki. I knew it! You really are Kim Dokja-nim!]
The dokkaebi greeted me with delight.
I vaguely remembered.
Youngki, the dokkaebi who had managed a subordinate channel under Bihyung.
[I heard rumors that you were alive, but to meet you in a place like this······!]
“Is Bihyung doing well?”
[He became noticeably downcast after you disappeared, Dokja-nim.]
Hearing that even Bihyung had become downcast made me feel a little guilty.
Apparently I'd grown attached to him along the way.
“You've cleaned up pretty well yourself. Back then, you didn't even know how to update a scenario.”
[Ahaha. How embarrassing, bringing up such ancient history······ I'm a full-fledged intermediate dokkaebi now.]
An intermediate dokkaebi.
This one had been part of the Korean Peninsula scenario too, so it seemed to have been promoted rapidly, like Bihyung. Still, I suddenly felt how much time had passed.
Even though all of that had happened less than a year ago.
[But, Dokja-nim. What do you mean when you say you'll sell the skill?]
Youngki, already watching me with calm eyes again.
Clueless or otherwise, a dokkaebi was still a dokkaebi.
I couldn't let my guard down here.
“Exactly what I said. I'll persuade the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint to sell her skill.”
[But how would you do that, Dokja-nim······?]
“I have my ways. What skill do you need? [Red Phoenix Shunpo]? Or [Hundred Steps Godly Fists]?”
[We already have Hundred Steps Godly Fists. What we need is······.]
“[Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship], then.”
At my words, Youngki nodded gravely.
Just as I'd thought.
Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship. The martial art that had bestowed the name Breaking the Sky (破天) upon the current Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
Yoo Joonghyuk's Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship was a martial art of the highest rank, one that anyone in <First Murim> would covet.
Seeing the Breaking the Sky Sword Master beside me about to growl, I hurriedly restrained it and spoke.
“All right. I'll sell it to you. Actually, I might even give it to you for free.”
At my words, the Breaking the Sky Sword Master looked up at me in disbelief.
Youngki also sounded startled as it asked,
[R-Really?]
“On the condition that you do me two favors. First······ offer [Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship] as a prize in the scenario you're opening soon.”
[Pardon?]
I smiled at the stupid look on Youngki's face.
This was [Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship], after all. Would I really just hand it over?
“You're holding a ‘Martial Arts Tournament scenario’ soon, aren't you? With [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] as a prize.”
[H-How did you know······!]
“Why are you so surprised? You do it all the time. It's a regular Murim scenario. A treasured sword appears, and every martial artist comes flocking in to fight tooth and nail for it.”
[That is true, but······ how did you know about Black Heavenly Demon Sword?]
How did I know?
The Martial Arts Tournament was one of the event scenarios Yoo Joonghyuk had participated in repeatedly whenever he visited <First Murim>.
I couldn't count how many comments I'd left begging the author to please skip the tournament.
“You don't need to know that. Anyway, offer the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's martial art as a prize too. Make it the first-place prize.”
Youngki's eyes darted rapidly.
It was probably a welcome proposal.

There were only so many things the dokkaebis could do after buying the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's martial art anyway. They could offer it as a prize in a large scenario to attract more subscribing constellations, or sell it at a high price through the Dokkaebi Bag.
Youngki was probably calculating which option would be more profitable.
[Very well. If you do that, I have nothing to lose. It would save us the cost of purchasing the martial art, too. However······.]
“However?”
[You said there were two favors, so I will decide after hearing the second condition as well.]
I smiled faintly at that caution.
Apparently becoming an intermediate dokkaebi had made it quite a bit smarter.
“The second condition is simple. Let everyone on this estate participate in the ‘Martial Arts Tournament scenario.’”
[Everyone on this estate······?]
Youngki's eyes narrowed.
Apparently it had finally caught on to my scheme.
[An interesting proposal, but······ that would be difficult.]
“Why?”
[The other incarnations are one thing, but the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint herself cannot participate.]
I'd expected that answer.

If the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint entered the Martial Arts Tournament, she would most likely win. Naturally, fewer people would enter, and the dokkaebis would have to take the loss. I spoke as though making a considerable concession.
“Then leave out the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.”
[In that case, very well. The Martial Arts Tournament scenario is in two weeks. Please have the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's skill ready by then.]
Youngki answered as though it had been waiting for that, and I responded in kind.
“All right. Just don't forget to send the scenario invitations properly.”
[Of course. Then I will see you again soon.]
“Give Bihyung my regards.”
[Haha, certainly.]

Apparently pleased that things had worked out, Youngki vanished with a delighted laugh. The dokkaebis accompanying it began to leave too. Paul glared at me right up until it left, so I glared back as fiercely as I could.
A little later, once all the dokkaebis had disappeared, Jang Hayoung tugged at my collar.
“Hey, what the hell did you just do? Sell the martial arts? Hold a tournament? What the hell are you······.”
Woof, woof! Woof, woof, woof!
「You would sell our martial arts! What on earth are you thinking?」
The Breaking the Sky Sword Master, which had been staring blankly at what I was doing, finally reacted too.
It was the reaction I'd expected.
Actually, this was probably mild by comparison.
“Kim Dokja!”

······Sure enough. Yoo Joonghyuk charged over in an enormous cloud of dust, grabbed me by the collar, and shook me as though I'd committed the greatest betrayal of his life. Flapping helplessly like a paper doll, I spoke.
“Let go so we can talk.”
“Shut up! What the hell are you thinking? Selling the martial arts······!”
“Calm down. I did it for you, you idiot.”
“Don't you know what we just got?”
At my words, Yoo Joonghyuk's hands finally stopped.
And then, a message that reached my ears.
[A new sub-scenario has arrived.]
[Sub-scenario― ‘Martial Arts Tournament’ is beginning.]
Yoo Joonghyuk fell silent for a moment, as though reading the details of the scenario that had arrived, then murmured quietly.
“······Black Heavenly Demon Sword?”
“Yeah. You said you wanted it.”
“Look closely, and there should be a Demon Spirit Bead too. Was that the third-place prize? I don't quite remember······.”
Yoo Joonghyuk's eyes wavered intensely as he looked at me.
His hands loosened, and he gently let go of me.
Come on, there was no need to be that moved.
Anyway, I seemed to have convinced one of them. The problem was the other one.
I turned my head to find the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint standing there with a rigid expression.
「Born with the divine power of a giant god (巨神). The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's very existence was no different from that of a god (神).」
There wasn't a single thing wrong with the description in Ways of Survival.
To think she could exert such pressure just by standing there.
I smiled politely and waved.
“Did your conversation with your disciple go well?”
“······So you're out of your mind.”
“Hear me out before you say that.”
“I have no time to waste words on some mere martial arts peddler.”
The mist around the barrier formation was thickening.
I hurriedly added,
“Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, you cannot cling to the old ways forever.”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's thick eyebrows curved menacingly.
“Is keeping that petty rule against teaching outsiders so important? Even if it means losing everything you have?”
Beside me, Yoo Joonghyuk looked at me as though I were a lunatic.
“Kim Dokja! Don't say another word!”
Of course, I kept running my mouth.

“[Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship] isn't even your real strength in the first place, is it? As you've transcended again and again, you must have discarded mere forms (形) long ago. What's so wrong with selling that paltry martial art?”
Rrrrrumble!
The ground all around us was shaking.
Finally, Yoo Joonghyuk shielded me behind his back and drew [Heavenly Sword of Gathering Clouds].
It felt as though gravity had intensified throughout the area.
Pain pressed down on me as though Mount Tai were crushing my shoulders. Beside me, Jang Hayoung and Han Myungoh were sinking into the ground, unable even to scream.
At this rate, our entire group would be wiped out.
“Master, wait······!”
Even at Yoo Joonghyuk's shout, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint didn't ease her pressure.
······So that's how you're going to play it? Stubborn as hell.
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ is activating a constellation's Status.]
Tzzzzzt!
Amid a storm of sparks, the gravity around us began to weaken temporarily. I grinned at the startled Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
My incarnation body might not amount to much, but I was a Narrative-grade constellation.
“I haven't even sold the martial art yet. Let's not be so harsh.”
“So you had a trick up your sleeve.”
“We can get the martial art back simply by winning the Murim tournament. It's just a tournament. All we have to do is win, isn't it?”
Tzzzz······.
Apparently she had calmed down a little, as the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's pressure eased considerably.
Of course, if she used her real power, subduing someone like me would be nothing. She was probably going easy on me because I was Joonghyuk's companion.
“Isn't this a tournament I can't enter anyway?”
“It's no fun when a grown adult barges into the children's game.”
“Murim's children are far stronger than you think.”
“I know. But your disciple is strong too.”
As the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint stood there as though wondering what I meant, I gave Yoo Joonghyuk's shoulder a couple of hearty pats.
“Our Joonghyuk will be entering the Martial Arts Tournament.”
At those words, Yoo Joonghyuk turned to me with his eyes wide.
I didn't know why he was so surprised by something so obvious.
Had he seriously thought I would enter?
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's eyebrows twitched once more.
“He's still weak.”
“Then you can make him strong. He's your disciple, after all.”
“I never said I would take him as my disciple······.”
This time, Yoo Joonghyuk stared wide-eyed at the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
Honestly, master and disciple were equally incapable of being honest.
[The exclusive skill ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’ is active.]
Of course, I knew full well that this inability to be honest was also one of their virtues.
「It's still far too early.」
「If he enters the tournament, Joonghyuk will die.」
「He's not at a level where he can compete with the ten greatest masters.」
Perhaps because my understanding was still low, I couldn't hear all of the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's thoughts. Even so, it wasn't difficult to work out what she was thinking.
In the end, I had to step in once again for this coy master and disciple.
“If you accept Yoo Joonghyuk as your disciple, I will arrange for you to meet your people.”
“······What do you mean?”
“The giants. Haven't you been searching for your people all this time?”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint stared at me as though looking at something strange.
“I don't know how you know that, but my people have been wiped from this world. There are no giants left anywhere.”
“No. There is still a place where they remain.”
I looked up into the air and spoke.
“Lord of the Underworld, are you still watching?”
As it happened, Hades was in my channel right now.
He'd helped me last time, so it was about time I greeted him properly.
But the one who answered my call wasn't Hades.
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ watches you with a curious smile.]
“······It has been a while, Persephone.”
Damn. This queen was tricky to deal with.
When on earth had she joined?
After cautiously gauging her reaction for a moment, I was about to speak when a message came.
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ says she has already heard the story.]
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ says she will grant your request.]
As always, I appreciated how quickly Persephone got to the point.
The problem was that this queen would never grant my request without an ulterior motive.
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ says she has a condition.]
······As expected.
“······Please, tell me.”
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ invites you to a festival of constellations.]
A festival of constellations?
Strange.
It shouldn't be time for the ‘Constellation Banquet’ yet, should it?
As though answering my question, Persephone sent another message.
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ has invited you to the ‘Gourmet Association (美食協).’]
From the following day, Yoo Joonghyuk devoted himself to training with the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.

Ever since hearing that she would be helped to find her people, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had worn a grave expression. Understanding how she felt, Yoo Joonghyuk refrained from offering careless consolation and instead sat cross-legged, immersing himself in meditation.
‘Originally, I intended to take her to meet the ancient giants myself, but······.’
Now that things had turned out this way, leaving it to Kim Dokja might not be so bad.
After all, meeting the ancient giants according to his original plan would require getting past at least the 40th scenario.
‘That guy. I never imagined he was so close to the Underworld.’
When he stopped to think about it, there were some things about Kim Dokja that he couldn't quite fathom.
How on earth did he manage to charm those cantankerous constellations so easily······?
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is grinning foolishly.]
That grinning archangel was a perfect example.
In the second round, the ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ hadn't been that sort of constellation.
A stern, exalted archangel burning with a sense of justice.
Yoo Joonghyuk couldn't understand why such a being had ended up like this in the current round.
“······Do you really intend to enter the tournament?”
At the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's question, Yoo Joonghyuk nodded silently.
“You could die. The Martial Arts Tournament scenario is no easy matter.”
“I am far stronger now than I was at this point in the previous round.”
“That still doesn't put you at a level where you can face the ten greatest masters.”
Yoo Joonghyuk knew Murim's ten greatest masters well.

The Ice Flower Goddess and Phantom Flyer, who sold their martial arts through merchants, were among them, and there was another such master in the Namgung Family, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's birth family (本家).
One of them might enter when the Martial Arts Tournament began.
Moreover, given the prizes in this tournament, he also had to consider the possibility that incarnations of famous constellations would enter.
[Several constellations are looking forward to the main rounds of the Martial Arts Tournament.]
[Some constellations are tired of the Martial Arts Tournament.]

One small mercy was that the more powerful constellations tended to grow bored with scenarios like this. Since the scenario repeated every year in Murim, constellations who had indulged in enough voyeurism at the ‘Murim tournament’ would probably pay it little attention.
After quietly checking Yoo Joonghyuk's pulse, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint spoke.
“You must unlock the second stage of Transcendent Form.”
“I have unlocked it before, so it should not be difficult.”
“It's different from breaking through the first stage.”
“I will manage somehow. I broke through the third stage in the previous round as well.”
“······The third stage?”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's pupils trembled faintly.

The third stage of Transcendent Form was not something talent alone could ever overcome. Breaking through it required an immense amount of ‘time.’ Yet there was no way Yoo Joonghyuk could have lived through that much time in the previous round······.
Understanding his master's question, Yoo Joonghyuk answered.
“I used the time fault in the Dark Dimension.”
The time fault in the Dark Dimension.
A place commonly called the ‘graveyard of martial artists.’
The martial artists who sought it out and entered could broadly be divided into two kinds.

Those who ran up against the wall set by their talent inside that prison of immense time and went mad, and those who broke through the wall after training that ate away at them and became transcendents.
Yoo Joonghyuk was the latter.
“······I can't even imagine how grueling your training must have been. How many years were you in there?”
“Probably about a hundred years.”
“The third stage in just a hundred years······ So that's why you've become so arrogant.”
A hundred years. A long time for an ordinary human, but not necessarily for a transcendent.

There were many in this world who failed to reach transcendence even after living and developing their martial arts for two hundred or three hundred years. A wall they couldn't cross even by stuffing themselves with every kind of elixir and improving their bodies. That was the thick wall of transcendence.
Yet Yoo Joonghyuk had crossed that wall three times in 100 years.
“If necessary, I intend to enter the time fault again in this round.”

“That's madness! Using the time fault taints your soul with impure energy. Haven't you seen the demonic masters who entered it and ended up insane? Don't you know by now that only a sheet of paper separates a madman from a transcendent?”
“······Even with the time fault, I could not surpass you in the previous round.”
“Hmph, of course not! You're still a hundred years too early to catch up to me!”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint spoke, still huffing.
“Anyway······ If you've broken through the third stage once, teaching you should at least be more rewarding than teaching someone who knows absolutely nothing.”
Yet despite his master's praise, Yoo Joonghyuk's expression remained gloomy. Sensing something amiss, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint questioned him, and he finally confessed.
A little later, after hearing the whole story, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint asked in disbelief.
“You attained profound enlightenment while you were exhausted?”
“Well, I do not remember exactly.”
In other words, he didn't know how he had crossed into the third stage.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint spoke incredulously.

“Don't tell me you're relying on your unconscious mind and confidently assuming you can break through the third stage again? That's the sort of nonsense only sham masters like the Ice Flower Goddess get up to.”
“That is why I need you. Please teach me martial arts again.”
“What?”
“The same method as before will not do. That would take too long.”
At her shameless disciple's words, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint pressed a hand to her temple.

“I don't know whether I'll be of any help. You've crossed the wall of transcendence yourself, so you should know: transcendence is never achieved through just one method. In the end, every transcendent ‘transcends’ in their own way.”
“Even so, you can help me. The saying ‘ten thousand streams return to one source (萬流歸宗)’ exists for a reason.”
“Ultimately, it means you must find one of those ten thousand paths. No two awakenings in the world are the same. Just as no two stories are the same.”
“Still, if there are ten thousand paths, might I not stumble upon at least one of them? I already found one in the previous round.”
As he said that, Yoo Joonghyuk somehow felt that he sounded like Kim Dokja. He wasn't normally the type to speak this way. Perhaps Kim Dokja had rubbed off on him while they traveled together.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint sighed at her disciple, who refused to concede a single point.
“······Were you always this talkative? It won't be easy. You should know from the previous round, but [Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship] was never meant for men.”
Yoo Joonghyuk knew that too.
It was why learning the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's martial arts had been so difficult in the previous round.
But this round was different.
“If gender is the problem, I can resolve it to some extent.”
“What does that mean?”
[A constellation who enjoys changing genders snorts.]
At the incoming indirect message, Yoo Joonghyuk frowned slightly.
Whenever this moment arrived, complicated emotions and immense anger welled up inside him. But now that things had come to this, he had to use everything at his disposal.
“As it happens, it is time.”
A moment later, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's mouth fell open in shock.
With an expressionless face, Yoo Joonghyuk drew his sword and wiped it as he spoke.
“You must never tell the guy outside.”
[Citizens who doubt your achievements are beginning to appear in the ‘Kim Dokja Industrial Complex’.]
[A Story about ‘Swindler Kim Dokja’ is spreading through the ‘Kim Dokja Industrial Complex’.]
The messages sounding from thin air woke me from my nap.
Judging by the wording of the messages, it seemed some nasty rumors were circulating in the industrial complex while I was away.
The industrial complex had a new ruler, but I still hadn't shown my face. In a way, it was only natural.
Still, ‘Swindler Kim Dokja’······.
Why did it feel as though people who didn't even know my face knew me better?
“Kim Dokja. What are you doing?”
A foot nudged me, and I groaned as I got up.
Yoo Joonghyuk stood there shirtless, drenched in sweat.
It looked as though he'd just come back from the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's grueling training.
“······I was just thinking for a minute.”
“You're slacking off.”
“I need to slack off right now. I'm a patient.”
It sounded like an excuse, but it was true.
I still hadn't fully recovered from the injuries caused by the ‘Exile Penalty’. Needlessly challenging the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had also done a lot to delay my recovery.
At least my proficiency in ‘Lamarck’s Giraffe’ was improving, and I was steadily consuming Story fragments, so my recovery shouldn't take too long.
I looked at the man and woman diligently practicing martial arts in the courtyard in front of the manor and asked,
“How are those two doing?”

There, an equally sweat-drenched Jang Hayoung was sparring with a miserable-looking Han Myungoh. The Breaking the Sky Sword Master, acting as their supervisor, barked away as it pointed out flaws in their moves.
“That girl has considerable talent. She's using a peculiar attribute to learn martial arts remarkably quickly.”
“Not a girl. He's a guy.”
“Sometimes I wonder where the hell your eyes are.”
What was this idiot talking about? He really was a guy, you know?
It said so in the original novel, too.
Just as I was about to snap back, Yoo Joonghyuk continued.
“More importantly, what happened with the constellations?”
“······I'm thinking it over.”
Before I knew it, a whole week had passed since I'd received Persephone's message.
[The constellation, ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’, has invited you to the ‘Gourmet Association (美食協)’.]
[In one week, the Gourmet Association's festival will be held at Oro Castle (五輅城) in the Dark Dimension.]
[By tonight, please decide whether you will depart.]
An invitation to the Gourmet Association.
I'd expected something like this might happen someday, but it had come far sooner than I'd anticipated.
The Gourmet Association (美食協).
Just as the name suggested, a gathering of constellations with discerning palates who loved fine food.
At first glance, it might seem similar to the ‘Constellation Banquet’, but the reality was entirely different.
While the ‘Constellation Banquet’ was an official gathering, the ‘Gourmet Association’ was unofficial, and the intensity of the events held there was on another level altogether.
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’, is worried about you.]
Above all, Uriel wasn't in the Gourmet Association.
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’, is curious about your choice.]
The Great Sage, Heaven's Equal wouldn't be there either, nor would the Secretive Plotter.
The Abyssal Black Flame Dragon······ had that one been there? I couldn't quite remember.

In any case, the atmosphere there wouldn't be entirely friendly toward me, the way it had been at the ‘Constellation Banquet’. And in the <Star Stream>, nothing was more dangerous than going somewhere full of unfriendly constellations.
Perhaps reading my expression, Yoo Joonghyuk asked,
“Are you scared?”
“Of course not.”

If something as trivial as that could keep me from attending the ‘Gourmet Association’, I could never have made it this far in the first place. I silently watched Jang Hayoung and Han Myungoh spar. Han Myungoh, taking blow after blow to the head, screamed as though adding a rhythm to the silence. Watching the same scene, Yoo Joonghyuk continued.
“It's because of this place.”
According to Persephone's message, the Gourmet Association's festival was exactly one week away.
And as luck would have it, that date coincided exactly with the ‘Martial Arts Tournament’.
In other words, I wouldn't be in the <First Murim> on the day the Martial Arts Tournament scenario began.
If something unexpected were to happen······.
“Go and come back, Kim Dokja.”
At Yoo Joonghyuk's firm words, I reflexively raised my head.
“······Will you be all right?”
“The scenario we're facing right now is the ‘Demon King Selection’, not the ‘Martial Arts Tournament’.”
I'd been thinking that all along, but hearing Yoo Joonghyuk say it filled me with a strange mixture of relief and pride.
“You······ really have become a decent human being. At least you won't die for a while.”
Yoo Joonghyuk ignored me and continued.
“The most we can get from the Martial Arts Tournament is the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword]. But getting the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] doesn't mean we can win the ‘Demon King Selection’.”
Yoo Joonghyuk was right.
Winning the ‘Murim Tournament’ certainly wouldn't mean we could win the ‘Demon King Selection’.
“That's why you have to go to the ‘Gourmet Association’. Our nebula needs companions. If you go to the Gourmet Association, you might be able to find allies.”
I understood what he meant.
Go to the Gourmet Association and sweet-talk some useful constellations into coming along.
But one word caught my attention.
“······Our nebula?”
“Didn't you say last time that you were going to make one?”
“Kim Dokja’s Company?”
“If it really has a name that lousy, I'll quit immediately.”
Yoo Joonghyuk, turning his head away with a fierce scowl.
A chuckle escaped me.
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’, wipes away tears of emotion with a handkerchief.]
I could never have imagined this when he first grabbed me by the collar.
To think that ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ and I had truly become companions.
In any case, now that Yoo Joonghyuk had gone so far as to say all that, it would be ridiculous for me to hesitate.
I got to my feet and said,
“I'll be back.”
That night, I welcomed the Gourmet Association's guide, who came flying through a portal.
Dressed like a cowboy straight out of a Western, the guide arrived driving a small carriage drawn by a black horse.
The guide seemed to be one of the retainers bound to the master of Oro Castle.
Stepping down from the carriage, the guide bowed politely to me before speaking.
[Are you the constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’-nim?]
“I am.”
[Please board the carriage. The journey will be rather long, so you are welcome to get some sleep.]
The guide showed no particular surprise or other notable reaction upon seeing me.
So someone who served as a guide for the Gourmet Association wouldn't be surprised by the likes of the ‘Demon King of Salvation’?
On the way to the driver's seat, the guide turned to ask,
[Other passengers will be joining us along the way. Would that be all right?]
“Oh, that's fine.”
Other passengers······ who could they be?
I wanted to ask, but the guide immediately set the carriage in motion, and I missed my chance.
Whatever it was made of, the carriage was quite spacious and comfortable inside. There wasn't the slightest jolting; I couldn't even feel the inertia that would tell me we were moving.
Perfect.
I could read some ‘Ways of Survival’ on the way.
For the next several hours, I read ‘Ways of Survival’ without stopping.
Perhaps it had been days rather than hours. Since I couldn't tell exactly how fast the carriage was moving, it was difficult for me to gauge the time.
「······And so, as the Yoo Joonghyuk of the 15th round lay dying, he thought, ‘Bad luck.’」
「······Ending his 19th round like that, Yoo Joonghyuk thought, ‘Next time.’」
「······As his 25th life came to an end, Yoo Joonghyuk muttered, “Next time, I'm really going.”」
······I took back what I'd said about him becoming a decent human being.
This bastard was still a sunfish, even in the First Revised Version.
Was he going to die all the same, whether I helped him or not?
As I skimmed past Yoo Joonghyuk's deaths, I didn't forget to look for the information I needed.
There wasn't much about the Gourmet Association.

Yoo Joonghyuk had visited the ‘Gourmet Association’ in one of his very late rounds, but he'd gone there to beat those bastards to death, not to make peace. That section was mostly riddled with “Aaaaargh!”
「Flying Fox said, “Constellations are all the worst. But the lunatics in the Gourmet Association are the worst of the worst.”」
Besides, there was hardly anything favorable to be found.
The more I read, the less certain I was that going to the Gourmet Association was the right thing to do.
In any case, I kept reading ‘Ways of Survival’.
「Yoo Joonghyuk thought, ‘I wish that guy had come with me.’」
If there was a difference in how the original and the revised version felt to read, it was when passages like this appeared.
Traces of the moments when I'd intervened in the original novel.
Whenever such passages appeared, I paid especially close attention.
They were among the few scenes that mentioned the story of the ‘3rd round’, which was absent from the revised version.
「‘But I have to do it this way. After all, that guy, too, said this was the right path.’」
······The right path? What was he talking about?
[It is mealtime. It is nothing special, but I have prepared a modest meal.]
“Thank you.”
Whenever the carriage stopped at intervals along the way, the guide brought me a meal.
It seemed to be a sort of in-flight meal.
It looked like jamón, a fine cured ham, and gave off a wonderfully fragrant aroma.
Of course, it wasn't real ham.
[The Last Gladiator of Planet Selegedon]
As expected of something provided by the Gourmet Association, even the in-flight meal was a Story.
Judging by the concentration of the Story I could sense, it seemed quite powerful······.
I sank the fork the guide had provided deep into the smooth flesh of the ham.
But at that moment, part of the Story's contents flowed into my mind.
―S-spare me. Please, spare me······!

A city being hideously torn apart amid the constellations' rampage. Incarnations crushed beneath immense pressure, their bodies bursting. A gladiator opposing them, stripped of all dignity and dying······.

The torn bodies of incarnations poured whole into the mouths of constellations laughing like demons. The final scene of a world that had already vanished. The incarnations' screams and despair gathered together, lingering at the tip of my nose.
I stared down at the ham for a moment, then quietly set down my fork.
[······Is the food not to your liking?]
“I'm not very hungry right now.”
I said it with a nonchalant smile.
[My apologies. It seems I failed to consider your preferences, constellation-nim. Some different food······.]
“No, I'll eat what I brought.”
Looking apologetic, the guide took the plate away and withdrew to the driver's seat.
Only when the guide was completely out of sight did I finally manage to let my expression relax.
I felt as though I was about to retch.
Suddenly, a passage from ‘Ways of Survival’ that I'd just read flashed through my mind.
「“It's a nightmare of a place for incarnations.”」
Once again, I realized just where I was going.
And who the beings I was dealing with were.
Like an idiot, I'd been acting as though I were going on a picnic.
I fiddled with a few Story fragments in my pocket.

Compared with the Stories those bastards ate, the Stories abandoned on the ‘Story Horizon’ were almost colorless and odorless. Unremarkable scraps of Stories about ordinary second- and third-rate incarnations who had lived ordinary lives and died.
There was a reason the Gourmet Association had discarded every one of them.
Absorbing those Story fragments through my hand with [Lamarck’s Giraffe], I quietly closed my eyes.
For some reason, I felt as though I would have a nightmare.
The journey continued for several days, and I used the spare time to tend to a few things I'd been unable to put in order.
[Coins held : 1,252,353 C]
First, I checked my coins, something I'd been too preoccupied to do for a while. When I looked, I found I'd accumulated a truly enormous sum.
1.25 million coins. That was enough to buy the [Great Demon's Eyes].
But Anna Croft had already bought that. I had a better skill, so I didn't particularly need it anyway······.
I considered how to use the remaining coins.

Raising my overall stats wouldn't be a bad idea, but once overall stats exceeded an average of 100, the returns actually began to drop sharply. From that point on, investing in skills was much better value for money than investing in overall stats.
Of course, overall stats could still prove useful when built up to overwhelming levels.
First, I'd have to persuade the ‘Fourth Wall’ to let me check my Attributes Window sometime soon.
[It seems the other passengers will be boarding now. Would that be all right?]
I'd been so deep in thought that I hadn't even noticed the carriage had stopped.
“Yes, that's fine.”
As I answered, the door on the left side of the carriage opened.
A little tense, I peered through the opening at the people about to join me.
After all, there was a good chance a constellation would be boarding.
“Ah! We've been waiting forever. Why are you so late?”
[My apologies. The road was somewhat rougher than expected······.]
The voice sounded strangely familiar.
A girl's high, thin voice with a Russian accent.
I could see three people in total through the opening.
[There is already a passenger aboard. I hope you all enjoy the journey.]
Whether that was fortunate or unfortunate, I couldn't sense the Status of a constellation.
In other words, they were all incarnations.
A woman approached with a gentle smile and boarded the carriage first.
“Please excuse me.”
The woman's khaki-brown hair fluttered in the breeze as she greeted me politely.
The moment she raised her head, I reflexively spoke.
“Selena Kim?”
Selena Kim.
She'd once attended the ‘Constellation Banquet’ as the representative of the United States.
Perhaps because my face had changed, the woman tilted her head for a moment before exclaiming.
“Do you remember who I am?”
“Of course! Kim Dokja! It's been a while! Were you invited, too?”
“That's how things worked out.”
As I shook hands with a delighted Selena Kim, I looked over the rest of her group.
Next to enter was a small girl with twin ponytails.
“Who are you······ huh?”
Sure enough, I'd seen this one before, too.
The Russian kid I'd met at the ‘Constellation Banquet’.
Her name······ what was it again? I remembered she'd had a nickname like Little Red Kid or something.
Ignoring the girl opening and closing her mouth at me, I turned to inspect the last person.
But at that moment, goosebumps broke out all down my spine.
“This is our first time meeting in person.”
That calm, unhurried voice held a depth that made the speaker's intentions impossible to fathom.
I knew this person well.
Someone counted alongside the Supreme King Yoo Joonghyuk as one of the strongest incarnations in ‘Ways of Survival’.
In fact, I'd even met this person before.
“I once saw you in a dream. It was so long ago that I wonder if you remember. I believe you told me then that we should meet again······.”
I remembered clearly.
During the ‘Green Zone’ scenario, I'd eaten a Specter's Stone and seen her.
“I remember.”
“Let me introduce myself properly. A pleasure to meet you, Kim Dokja. No······ ‘Demon King of Salvation’.”
Between strands of fluttering blond hair, a swirling yellow demon eye (魔眼) smiled quietly.
It was an exceptionally beautiful smile, but I couldn't take it at face value. I knew better than anyone the sinister ideology concealed behind it.
“I'm Anna Croft.”
The Prophet of Asgard.
Anna Croft, the leader of ‘Zarathustra’, was there.
